subject.title: feat: keep main agents aware of group activity

question: Should a same-agent main session automatically receive durable, read-only visibility into human activity from every eligible group session when effective `dmScope` is `main`?
rationale: This is a new cross-session visibility contract with user-context and privacy implications; source-level guards can constrain implementation but cannot determine whether this ambient access model is the intended product behavior.

options.title: Approve ambient same-agent visibility
options.body: Accept the new queue-only, read-only ambient watch model after final lifecycle and live-behavior proof confirms it does not broaden access beyond eligible same-agent groups.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep current isolation by default and expose an explicit session or policy opt-in before granting main-session reads of group activity.

options.title: Narrow the feature
options.body: Limit automatic watches to a smaller set of group/session modes if broad same-agent visibility is not the desired privacy contract.

recommendation.title: Approve ambient same-agent visibility
recommendation.body: Accept the new queue-only, read-only ambient watch model after final lifecycle and live-behavior proof confirms it does not broaden access beyond eligible same-agent groups.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commit series shows this person authored the complete proposed session and routing design; no stronger current-main ownership trail could be established in the read-only environment.
